title: Capability envelope API: canonical schema for onboarding profiles, limits, and version binding
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define and publish a single canonical API schema that exposes a model's capability envelope (features, hard limits, recommended context sizes, and operational constraints) to support deterministic onboarding and version pinning. This ticket scopes the schema design, backwards compatibility rules, and the wire contract for both the public Redwood API and internal model-catalog ingestion job. The goal is to enable clients and the Console to programmatically discover: supported features (chat, streaming, tool-calling), token and context limits (max_tokens, recommended_window_by_profile), latency profile hints, quantization compatibility flags, and pinned-version metadata with deprecation windows.
acceptance_criteria:
- A JSON schema (draft) documented and committed to the spec repo describing: features, limits, profiles (production/dev/burst), version bindings, and deprecation metadata.
- API endpoints defined: GET /models/{model_id}/capability-envelope and GET /models/{model_id}/profiles returning the canonical payload.
- Integration test that validates schema against two sample model manifests (an open Llama variant and a proprietary quantized variant).
- Console wire contract PR drafted + migration notes for existing model-catalog consumers.
- Feature flag to toggle new endpoint for gradual rollout.
design_notes:
Key design choices: (1) Use a small set of orthogonal primitives instead of monolithic 'capabilities' blobs so clients can merge defaults, overrides, and profile-specific hints. (2) Profile objects are first-class: each profile contains a machine-readable stable id, user-facing label, numeric limits, and recommended runtime knobs (batch_size, kv_cache_policy). (3) Version binding uses an explicit 'pinned_version' field with a 'pin_type' enum (exact | semver_semver_range | latest_compatible) and 'deprecation_date' to enable automated rollout tooling. (4) Keep 'latency_hint' as coarse buckets (realtime|interactive|batch) to avoid noisy per-model SLAs in the catalog.

Compatibility: the schema must be additive-only for the next two releases; new optional fields allowed, but renames or removals require migration path. This matches the platform's upgrade semantics for hosted and dedicated customers.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (schema spec + tests, 1 sprint): write JSON Schema, wire up ingestion job to emit capability-envelopes into model-catalog topic, add integration test fixtures.
Phase 2 (API + Console, 1 sprint): implement read endpoints in catalog service, surface in Console model details page behind flag, publish SDK helpers.
Phase 3 (rollout, 2 sprints): enable feature flag for internal accounts, gather telemetry for mismatched expectations, iterate on defaults, then flip to public.

Rollback plan: keep old /models/{id}/manifest endpoint unchanged; new endpoint is additive. If regressions occur, revert catalog-to-catalog-topic commit and disable flag; existing clients unaffected.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: clients assume numeric limits are hard limits when some models use 'recommended_context' vs enforced 'max_tokens'. Mitigation: provide explicit 'limit_type' for each numeric field (hard|recommended) and update SDKs to surface both.
- Risk: version pin semantics differ between private deployments and hosted; Mitigation: expose 'pin_scope' (hosted|dedicated|private) and document behavior.
- Risk: large schemas increase manifest size; Mitigation: allow condensed 'profile_refs' for published manifests and expand on-demand in the catalog service.
